column1: # Third-party artifacts. Tab-separated: name, url, sha256.
# sha256 of TOFU means "not yet known" -- the checksum is computed and
# pinned on first fetch, and the change is committed deliberately.
# The two Tier 2 entries below (utm-bundle, opencore-legacy-img) are
# evidence, not ingredients: someone else's blobs, never in the repo, and
# nothing the plugin builds or boots references them (INGREDIENTS.md,
# "Provenance"; docs/decisions/0004).
# name
utm-bundle
opencore-legacy-img
opencorepkg-src
# The OpenCore build's other inputs. Upstream's build_oc.tool curls
# ocbuild's efibuild.sh off master and evals it, and that script clones
# acidanthera/audk at master; both are pinned here instead.
# The audk-* entries after audk-src are audk's own submodules, at the
# commits its gitlinks name. A GitHub archive tarball carries no submodule
# content, and EDK II's build.py validates every [Includes] path in every
# .dec it parses, so the whole set is fetched rather than only the two that
# get compiled. internal/firmware/pins.go declares which commit each one is
# pinned to, and mavericks-firmware refuses a URL here that names a
# different one (firmware.CheckPins).
ocbuild-efibuild
audk-src
audk-openssl
audk-brotli
audk-mbedtls
audk-oniguruma
audk-libfdt
audk-mipisyst
audk-jansson
audk-libspdm
audk-cmocka
audk-googletest
audk-subhook
# SMC emulation kexts, injected by OpenCore. Tier 1: acidanthera release
# binaries, pinned to an exact release tag (never "latest") and checksummed.
# We do not build these from source; assets/firmware/README.md records why these
# versions and how their 10.9 (Darwin 13) support was verified.
lilu-release
virtualsmc-release
# Apple. Mavericks 10.9.5 InstallESD.dmg, the one thing here that may not
# come from anywhere else. lib/vendor.sh's fetch_source cannot fetch it:
# the URL below is Apple's real one, but it answers only with an
# AssetToken cookie obtained from osrecovery.apple.com. mavericks-installesd
# does that handshake and checks this checksum -- the transfer is plain
# HTTP, so the checksum is the only integrity there is. Recorded here so
# the registry names every third-party artifact, including the one a plain
# download cannot get.
apple-installesd-10.9.5
# Apple's post-10.9.5 standalone updates, fetched from Apple's own CDN and
# pinned by checksum. The template's updates variable chooses which of
# these a guest carries: none, security or all (docs/decisions/0011).
# These are NEVER republished -- they are fetched at build time, on the
# user's machine, from Apple, exactly like apple-installesd-10.9.5 above.
# bin/no-apple-bytes.sh is the gate.
# NEVER run `softwareupdate` at build time to get these. That reaches
# Apple's servers during the build, makes the build non-reproducible and
# network-dependent, and a 2013 OS talking to 2026 servers may hang.
# Pinned standalone packages exist precisely to avoid it.
# Every URL and size here was taken from Apple's own
# index-10.9.merged-1.sucatalog on 2026-09-22 and every byte count matched
# the KiB figure the guest's own `softwareupdate -l` printed on 2026-09-21.
# updates = "security" installs this one, and it is the default.
# Receipt identifier: com.apple.pkg.update.security.2016-004Mavericks.13F1911
# It carries SystemVersion.plist, so the guest's ProductBuildVersion moves
# 13F34 -> 13F1911 while ProductVersion stays 10.9.5. It also replaces
# /usr/bin/ssh and /usr/sbin/sshd, which is why firstboot.sh installs the
# updates BEFORE the family's OpenSSH rather than after.
apple-secupd-2016-004
# updates = "all" adds these. They are applications rather than the OS, which
# is why they are opt-in. iTunes 12.6.2 is one softwareupdate product made
# of five flat packages; they are listed here in the order the product's
# own Packages array gives, which is the order they must be installed in.
apple-safari-9.1.3
apple-itunes-12.6.2-corefp
apple-itunes-12.6.2-mobiledevice
apple-itunes-12.6.2-itunesaccess
apple-itunes-12.6.2-itunesx
apple-itunes-12.6.2-coreadi
# Mac OS X 10.6's updates, for snowleopard-media's updates = "security" (the
# default): Apple's client 10.6.8 combo update, then 10.6's last security
# update. Same rules as 10.9's above: fetched at build time from Apple's
# servers on the user's machine, never republished, never by
# `softwareupdate`.
# The combo is the catalogue product 041-98179 in Apple's
# index-leopard-snowleopard.merged-1.sucatalog, read 2026-10-04, every size
# matching the catalogue's: its distribution and the 18 packages beside it,
# which the distribution installs in ONE installer run (firstboot.sh runs
# `installer -pkg <the .dist>`). MEASURED 2026-10-04: installed one at a
# time instead, its SUBaseSystem package brings a new libSystem while dyld
# stays 10.6.0's, and every process after it crashes. The distribution
# itself picks the Rosetta, QuickTime 7 and X11 packages by what the guest
# has. (The catalogue's other 10.6.8 combo, 041-98121, is client and
# server in one, with an unconditional server package; not this one.)
apple-combo-10.6.8-part0
apple-combo-10.6.8-part1
apple-combo-10.6.8-part2
apple-combo-10.6.8-part3
apple-combo-10.6.8-part4
apple-combo-10.6.8-part5
apple-combo-10.6.8-part6
apple-combo-10.6.8-part7
apple-combo-10.6.8-part8
apple-combo-10.6.8-part9
apple-combo-10.6.8-part10
apple-combo-10.6.8-part11
apple-combo-10.6.8-part12
apple-combo-10.6.8-subasesystem
apple-combo-10.6.8-qt7
apple-combo-10.6.8-x11
apple-combo-10.6.8-rosetta
apple-combo-10.6.8-meta
apple-combo-10.6.8-dist
# Security Update 2013-004 for 10.6.8, the client product (041-91751); the
# catalogue's other one (041-91749) adds the server package.
apple-secupd-2013-004-snowleopard
